The petitioners of MVC No.4775/2023 c/w. 4776/2023 have filed these petitions under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1989 seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by them in the road traffic accident occurred on 22.06.2023.

sentences.text: The petitioner of MVC No.4775/2023 has filed application to club MVC No.4776/2023 with it.
The said application came to be allowed on the ground that the respondents in both the cases are one and the same and the injuries were caused from the same accident.
Hence, both these cases are clubbed together to lead common evidence.
3. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners as follow:-

On 22.06.2023 at about 5.15 p.m. when they were travelling in a Private Bus bearing Reg. No. KA-51-AG-206 as passengers, on Manvi Sindanur road, near Nasalapur bridge, Manvi Taluk,
Raichur District, the driver of the said bus driven the same with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the motor cycle which was coming from opposite direction.

After hitting the motor cycle, the driver lost control over the bus and then hit the safety iron sheet fixed on side of the road, caused the accident and as a result, they sustained grievous injuries.

It is contended that, immediately they were taken to nearby Govt. hospital, Manvi, wherein they were taken first aid, thereafter for higher treatment they were shifted to Fortis hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein they took treatment as an inpatient.
It is  SCCH-08 4 MVC No.4775/2023 c/w. 4776/2023 contended that they have spent huge amount for treatment and medical expenses.

4. It is further stated that prior to the accident, petitioners in MVC No.4775/2023 and 4776/2023 were hale and healthy and petitioner in MVC No.4775/20223 was owner cum driver of 407 Goods vehicle and was earning sum of Rs.50,000/- p.m. and the petitioner in MVC No.4776/2023 was working as Electrician and was earning sum of Rs.24,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries, they are unable to do their work as doing earlier.

It is stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the private bus bearing Reg.
No. KA-51-AG-206.
Hence, the 1st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
5. Inspite of service of summons, the 1 st respondent remained exparte.
On service of notice, 2 nd respondent appeared before the court through its counsel and filed separate written statements.

sentences.text: The 2nd respondent in its objections has stated that the petitions are not maintainable either in law or on facts and hence the petitions are liable to be dismissed for non joinder of necessary parties.

This respondent has denied the issuance of policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of the offending Bus bearing Reg No.
KA-51-AG-0206 and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.

Further stated that, the petitioners sustained injuries due to the negligent act of the rider of motor cycle who was riding the said motor cycle in a rash and negligent  SCCH-08 5 MVC No.4775/2023 c/w. 4776/2023 manner on narrow Bridge.
Further stated that the rider of the motor cycle was not having DL and policy in respect of motor cycle.
The police authorities not complied the provisions as contemplated u/s 158(6) of MV Act.
Further stated that the owner of the bus allowed many persons to travel in the bus exceeding its capacity and violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further stated that the driver of the private bus was driving the vehicle without possessing a valid and effective driving licence, FC and Permit.
It has denied the age, occupation and income, period of hospitalization and treatment taken by the petitioners.
It is contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is high exorbitant.
On other grounds pray for dismissal of the petitions.

7. Based on the pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed following issues :-
 ISSUES IN MVC NO.4775/2023 & 4776/2023  1. Whether the petitioners prove that on 22.06.2023 at  about 5.15 p.m. when they were travelling as  passenger in the bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AG-206,
 on Manvi Sindanur road, near Nasalapur Bridge,
 Manvi Taluk, Raichur District, at that time, the  driver of the said bus drove the same with high speed  and in a rash and negligent manner and hit against  the motor cycle which was coming from opposite  direction, thereafter lost control and dashed to the  safety iron sheet fixed on side of the road and finally  fell down to road side deep area, due to which they  sustained injuries?
 2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for  compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from  whom?
 3. What order or award?

 REASONS 11. Issue No.1 in both the cases:
The averments stated in the petitions and facts stated in examination-in-chief of P.W.1 and PW.2 filed by way of affidavit are one and the same.
Therefore, for the purpose of brevity, it is not necessary to explain once again the facts as stated in the affidavit.

The PW.1 has produced F.I.R, F.I.S, Spot Mahazar, IMV report,
Wound certificate and charge sheet as per Ex.P1 to 6.

On the other hand, respondent No.2 examined one witness as RW.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.D.1 and Ex.D.2.
 12.

According to the version of petitioners in both the cases,
the accident happened on Manvi Sindanur road, near Nasalapur  SCCH-08 7 MVC No.4775/2023 c/w. 4776/2023 bridge, Manvi Taluk, Raichur District, they were traveling in Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AG-206 as passengers at that time, the driver of the bus drove it with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the motor cycle which was coming from opposite direction.
After hitting the motor cycle, the driver lost control over the bus and then hit the safety iron sheet fixed on side of the road, due to which petitioners sustained injuries.
It is pertinent to note that, the criminal law was set in motion on the same day of accident as per Ex.P.2. Ex
. P.1 FIR has its germane in Ex.P.2.

The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P.3 the Spot Mahazar and also Sketch which was Jagadish vs Umesh .M.A on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156609691/
5 prepared at the time of Spot Mahazar.
On close perusal of the Ex.P.3 it reflects that the injured were traveling in the Bus as a passengers and accident occurred near Nasalapura Bridge as per Ex.P3 which is mahazar and Sketch.

As per these documents the said road is slightly curve road, the driver of the Bus drove it in a negligent manner with high speed and dashed against one motorcycle which was coming in the opposite direction and then lost his control over bus and hit the safety iron sheet and the said place is bridge.

If the driver of the bus drove it in a normal speed by observing on going vehicles on the road and also curve and bridge,
then he would certainly avoided the accident.
Added more, the contents of Ex.P4 which is the IMV report itself discloses that there are no mechanical defects whatsoever in the offending vehicle.
Further more, even the chargesheet as per Ex.P6 was also filed as against the driver of the bus.
When such is the case having regard to Ex.P3 and 4 coupled with Ex.P6 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the Bus driver.
In the arguments counsel of respondent raised  SCCH-08 8 MVC No.4775/2023 c/w. 4776/2023 the point that there was negligence on the part of rider of the motorcycle who came from opposite side.
The petitioners have not made them as party, who is also necessary party in this petition.
The petitioners are the eye witnesses to the accident.

The respondents have failed to elicit anything in their defence from the mouth of petitioners who deposed that the accident occurred only due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the bus and the respondents have not examined the eye witness of the accident.
Hence, the said contention of the respondents is not proper.
13. The driver of the bus has not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part.

After the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of the Bus bearing registration No.KA-51-MG-5501 concluding that the accident was occurred only due to his negligence.
There is no reason to take a different view.
Therefore, I hold that the accident was occurred only due to the rash and negligent act of driver of the offending Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MG-5501.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in all the cases in the Affirmative.
ISSUE No.2 in MVC 4775/2023:
14. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS ON ACCOUNT OF  PERMANENT DISABILITY:

It is the case of the petitioner that prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and he was owner cum driver of 407 Goods vehicle and earning Rs.50,000/- per month, but there is no any document towards proof of income.

Hence, in the absence of document of income, the tribunal has to consider the notional Jagadish vs Umesh .M.A on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156609691/
6 income of the petitioner.
The incident occurred during the year  SCCH-08 9 MVC No.4775/2023 c/w. 4776/2023 2023.
considering the avocation and the year of the accident, I deem it just and proper to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,000/- per month.
The petitioner claims that he is unable to work due to the injuries sustained to him.
The petitioner got examined the Doctor Avinash Parthasarathy as PW.4.

In the evidence of doctor, he has deposed that petitioner sustained fracture shaft of femur right side and the petitioner has undergone surgery of CR and IM nailing for femur fracture and got discharged with an advise to take follow up treatment.

On examination, the petitioner complains of pain in right hip, thigh, knee and stiffness in right hip and knee and unable to walk or sit normally, climb stairs and it is found that the petitioner has Antalgic gait in right lower limb, tenderness over right thigh, hip and knee and Arc of movement of right knee restricted, Arc of movement of right hip flexion restricted, rotation restricted and abduction/adduction restricted, difficulty in walking,
climbing stairs, squatting, sitting cross legged, kneeling and turning and X-ray shows old right femur fracture with implant in situ.
He assessed 18% disability to the whole body disability of the petitioner.
While calculating the loss of future income on account of permanent disability, the functional disability to the whole body has to be considered.
The disability to the whole body shall have to be assessed on the basis of the profession of the injured and relative effect of the disability to his profession.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner are not in dispute and the injuries sustained by him definitely will have an impact on his work.
PW.4 is not a treated doctor and the disability assessed by him has to be  SCCH-08 10 MVC No.4775/2023 c/w. 4776/2023 taken into consideration carefully.
Hence, considering the nature of the work and impact of disability on his performance, I deem it just and proper to consider 12% disability to his whole body.
It is contended that petitioner was aged 47 years as on the date of accident.
The accident occurred on 22.06.2023.

However,
by considering the date of birth mentioned in Ex.P7 Adhaar card as 10.06.1976, the petitioner was aged 47 years at the time of accident.
The multiplier applicable to the age of 47 is 13 as per the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation(AIR 2009 SC 3104).

sentences.text: 15. PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
The wound certificate marked at Ex.P5 discloses the injuries sustained by the petitioner.

Further the Ex.P11 Discharge Summary of Fortis Hospital reveals that petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital from 23.06.2023 to 26.06.2023 and underwent closed reduction and internal fixation with femur interlock nail.
Considering these aspects, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.50,000/- towards pain and sufferings.
16. MEDICAL EXPENSES:

The petitioner has produced medical bills worth Rs.44,915/-
as per Ex.P12.
I have examined the medical bills and receipts.

Since the petitioner was treated as inpatient and undergone  SCCH-08 11 MVC No.4775/2023 c/w. 4776/2023 treatment, there are no reasons to disbelieve the amount spent by the petitioner to the tune of Rs.44,915/- and he is entitled for the same.
17. ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD & NOURISHMENT  AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:

As the petitioner was treated as an inpatient for a period of 4 days, certainly he might have spent amount towards conveyance,
attendant charges, nourishing food and other incidental expenses and also at the time of subsequent follow up treatment.

Considering these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.5,000/-
under this head.
18. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 4 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.64,000/- (16,000X4)
under this head.

FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:

Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the Private bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-AG-0206.
The respondent No.2 has not proved the breach of any of the policy conditions.
Hence, 1 st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 2nd respondent being the insurer shall indemnify the 1 st respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative in MVC No.4775/2023 and MVC No.4776/2023.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioners of MVC No.4775/2023 c/w. 4776/2023 have filed these petitions under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1989 seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by them in the road traffic accident occurred on 22.06.2023.
The petitioner of MVC No.4775/2023 has filed application to club MVC No.4776/2023 with it.
After hitting the motor cycle, the driver lost control over the bus and then hit the safety iron sheet fixed on side of the road, caused the accident and as a result, they sustained grievous injuries.
Due to the accidental injuries, they are unable to do their work as doing earlier.
Hence, the 1st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

opennyai_summary.issue:
7. Based on the pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed following issues :-
 ISSUES IN MVC NO.4775/2023 & 4776/2023  1. Whether the petitioners prove that on 22.06.2023 at  about 5.15 p.m. when they were travelling as  passenger in the bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AG-206,
 on Manvi Sindanur road, near Nasalapur Bridge,
 Manvi Taluk, Raichur District, at that time, the  driver of the said bus drove the same with high speed  and in a rash and negligent manner and hit against  the motor cycle which was coming from opposite  direction, thereafter lost control and dashed to the  safety iron sheet fixed on side of the road and finally  fell down to road side deep area, due to which they  sustained injuries?
 2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for  compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from  whom?
 3. What order or award?
 SCCH-08 6 MVC No.4775/2023 c/w. 4776/2023 Jagadish vs Umesh .M.A on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156609691/

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
When such is the case having regard to Ex.P3 and 4 coupled with Ex.P6 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the Bus driver.
The petitioners are the eye witnesses to the accident.
The respondents have failed to elicit anything in their defence from the mouth of petitioners who deposed that the accident occurred only due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the bus and the respondents have not examined the eye witness of the accident.
After the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of the Bus bearing registration No.KA-51-MG-5501 concluding that the accident was occurred only due to his negligence.
Therefore, I hold that the accident was occurred only due to the rash and negligent act of driver of the offending Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MG-5501.
The disability to the whole body shall have to be assessed on the basis of the profession of the injured and relative effect of the disability to his profession.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner are not in dispute and the injuries sustained by him definitely will have an impact on his work.
PW.4 is not a treated doctor and the disability assessed by him has to be  SCCH-08 10 MVC No.4775/2023 c/w. 4776/2023 taken into consideration carefully.
Hence, considering the nature of the work and impact of disability on his performance, I deem it just and proper to consider 12% disability to his whole body.
Since the petitioner was treated as inpatient and undergone  SCCH-08 11 MVC No.4775/2023 c/w. 4776/2023 treatment, there are no reasons to disbelieve the amount spent by the petitioner to the tune of Rs.44,915/- and he is entitled for the same.
It is the case of the petitioner that prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and he was working as Electrician and earning Rs.24,000/- per month, but there is no any document towards proof of income.
The incident occurred during the year 2023.
He assessed 10% permanent physical impairment in the LS spine of the petitioner.
While calculating the loss of future income on account of permanent disability, the functional disability to the whole body has to be considered.
The disability to the whole body shall have to be assessed on the basis of the profession of the injured and relative effect of the disability to his profession.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner are not in dispute and the injuries sustained by him definitely will have an impact on his work.
PW.4 is not a treated doctor and the disability assessed by him has to be taken into consideration carefully.
Hence, considering the nature of the work and impact of disability on his performance, I deem it just and proper to consider 5% disability to his whole body.
The accident occurred on 22.06.2023.
However,
by considering the year of birth mentioned in Ex.P14 Adhaar card as 1968, the petitioner was aged 55 years at the time of accident.
The multiplier applicable to the age of 55 is 11 as per the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation(AIR 2009 SC 3104).
Jagadish vs Umesh .M.A on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156609691/
10  Hence, petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.1,05,600/-(Rs.16,000x12x11x5/100) towards loss of future income on account of permanent disability.

Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated Jagadish vs Umesh .M.A on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156609691/
12 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% p.a.
